candidate_relations.reason: Conjunctival lipogranuloma involves lipid-laden granulomatous inflammation, not amyloid protein deposition. The clinical features (pinkish-yellow mass, CT isodense to muscle, foreign body sensation) are more consistent with amyloidosis than lipogranuloma, and the two are distinct pathological entities.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Lipogranuloma is a granulomatous reaction to lipid material, distinct from amyloid deposition

candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record specifies a purely conjunctival mass in the lower fornix with pinkish-yellow coloration (distinguishing it from lymphoid salmon-pink lesions), no systemic disease, normal labs, and CT showing a homogeneous mass isodense to muscle confined to the conjunctiva — all hallmark features of localized conjunctival amyloidosis. The anatomical qualifier 'conjunctival' is fully supported by the record and represents the complete diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Conjunctival amyloidosis is the anatomically specified form of the reference diagnosis amyloidosis in this ocular context

candidate_relations.scope_detail: Conjunctival fibroma is a benign fibrous tumor, a distinct entity from amyloidosis
